contemporary

/kuhn-TEM-puh-rer-ee/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something that is contemporary belongs to the present time or era.

The museum's contemporary art wing features works made within the last decade.

Example

Past the marble statues and Renaissance oil paintings, the museum's newest wing feels like another world of contemporary art: video installations, 3D-printed sculptures, and canvases finished within the last few years by artists who are still working today.

The new wing's art belongs to our own moment in time, which is exactly what contemporary means. It is more precise than 'new' because contemporary locates something in the present era, not merely something recently made.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

present-day: Present-day is a plain time-stamp meaning existing in our own time, as in present-day Tokyo. Contemporary can say that too, but it also carries the flavor of current style -- contemporary art, contemporary music -- and can even mean living at the same time as someone else.

current: Current means happening or in use right now -- the current schedule, the current champion. Contemporary is wider: it places something in the whole present era, with its styles and concerns, not just this moment. A bus timetable is current; a story full of smartphones is contemporary.

up-to-date: Up-to-date means reflecting the latest information or style -- records or software that have kept pace. Contemporary means belonging to the present era itself. Something old can be brought up-to-date with edits and patches; something contemporary was made in, and belongs to, our own moment.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

ancient: from the very distant past

old-fashioned: no longer in current style

Where it sits · how close to right now it is

recent → modern → contemporary → cutting-edge

recent vs. contemporary: Recent is weaker than contemporary — recent means from a short while ago, while contemporary means belonging fully to the present moment.

modern vs. contemporary: Modern is slightly weaker than contemporary; modern covers a broad recent era, but contemporary points to what exists right now, today.

cutting-edge vs. contemporary: Cutting-edge is stronger than contemporary — contemporary things belong to the present, while cutting-edge things push beyond the present to the newest frontier.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — con-: together, with (Latin)

root — tempor: time (Latin (tempus))

suffix — -ary: relating to (Latin)

Put it together: Con- (together with) + tempor (time) + -ary (relating to): contemporary literally means 'sharing the same time' — belonging to the present time or era.

Use the root in a new word: temporary: A temporary fence went up around the ball field this week.

Root Check

Word Choice

Contemporary works two ways depending on context: describing something current and modern (contemporary music, contemporary issues) or describing something that existed at the same time as something else (a writer contemporary with Shakespeare) — the surrounding sentence usually makes clear which sense is meant.
